_comment: Polarization-resolved two-colour MFD (multi-parameter fluorescence detection). Four detection channels = spectral (green/red) x polarization (parallel/perpendicular), simulation channels 0..3 in the order green-par, green-perp, red-par, red-perp. Map them onto instrument routing channels with `tttr sim --channels 4 --routing-channels 0,8,1,9` and read them back with examples/simulation/configs/mfd_detector_setups.json, whose `green` is {0,8} and `red` is {1,9}. Two doubly-labelled species differing in FRET efficiency AND in rotational freedom: species 1 is low-FRET (E~0.2) and slowly tumbling (long donor lifetime 3.8 ns, high residual anisotropy), species 2 is high-FRET (E~0.8) and fast tumbling (donor lifetime 1.6 ns, low anisotropy). The per-channel brightness rows carry the anisotropy: for a parallel/perpendicular pair with fundamental anisotropy r, the steady-state split is (1+2r)/3 parallel and (1-r)/3 perpendicular per polarization arm, so a burst's (par - perp)/(par + 2 perp) recovers r. Species 1 uses r = 0.30, species 2 r = 0.10. BACKGROUND: uncorrelated background is FLAT in micro time, and saying so is not optional. With `background` set and no `background_decay`, the engine writes micro-time channel 0 for every background photon -- which is what *scatter* looks like -- and any lifetime fit then recovers a large fake scatter component (see BUGS.md). One bin as wide as the laser period IS flat: a pattern is sampled uniformly *within* its bin, so `{"pattern": [1.0], "dt": 32.0}` draws a micro time uniform over [0, 32) ns.
